subject: SOC 2 evidence request and hosting jurisdiction
messages:
From: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@whiteco.eu>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@whiteco.eu
Date: 2026-07-20T08:32:00Z
Subject: SOC 2 evidence request and hosting jurisdiction

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — WhiteCo's procurement/security teams are collecting final evidence before we move to contract. We have a few urgent asks:

- Can you provide your SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) and confirm the audit period it covers?
- Do you have a bridge letter we can rely on if the audit period doesn't align with our renewal window (we need assurance through 2026-08-31)?
- For EU customers, we need confirmation of hosting jurisdiction and any cross-border transfers. Specifically: where is customer content stored at rest and where is it processed?
- Do you execute the standard EU SCCs in your DPA? Is there a KMS/customer-managed key option?
- What logs are retained (duration) and do server logs include customer PII?

We'd like to triage quickly; please attach anything you can share and let us know if you prefer a short call with our security lead.

Best,
Claire
Claire Dubois
Head of Information Security, WhiteCo

Attachments: none
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@whiteco.eu>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-20T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence request and hosting jurisdiction

Hi Claire — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful.

Short answers up front: we can share our SOC 2 Type II report and a draft bridge letter; we support EU-hosted deployments and have contractual SCCs/DPA; customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated/Private deployments; logs default to 90 days but that is configurable. See attached artifacts for the SOC 2 report and a bridge-letter template.

A couple of points to clarify so we give you a clean answer: are you evaluating our Hosted (multi-tenant API) offering or would you require Dedicated / Private hosting (single-tenant or VPC)? For Hosted customers we run an EU region (eu-central-1) for data residency on request, but certain control-plane services and some back-office telemetry are operated from our US control plane. For Dedicated/Private we can provide full EU-only data plane + customer KMS and tighter contractual residency guarantees.

If you can confirm the deployment model WhiteCo prefers, Jonás (copied) will follow with technical specifics and Marissa will propose the contractual language and timeline for a DPA + bridge letter.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow or Thursday to close this out?

Regards,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@whiteco.eu>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-21T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence request and hosting jurisdiction

Hi Claire — Jonas from Redwood security here, following up with the technical details Laura promised. Apologies for the longer reply, I wanted to include specifics for procurement/security review.

1) SOC 2 Type II report: attached (covers 2025-01-01 through 2025-06-30). The report is certified by an independent third party.

2) Bridge letter: we maintain a standard bridge-letter template that attests to no material control changes since the last report; we can provide a signed bridge letter to extend assurances through 2026-08-31 subject to legal sign-off. See attached draft.

3) Hosting / processing / transfers:
- Hosted (self-serve API): We provide region selection at account creation. If WhiteCo requests EU-only data residency, customer content (data-at-rest and data-inference processing) will be stored and processed in eu-central-1 (AWS Frankfurt).
- Control plane: administrative/control-plane services (account management, billing metadata, some telemetry) are operated from our US control plane. Control-plane metadata does not include customer content, though it may contain non-sensitive usage metrics.
- Dedicated / Private: For Dedicated and Private deployments we can commit to EU-only control plane and data plane (on-prem or VPC), with customer-managed KMS.
- Cross-border transfers: For Hosted customers who select EU residency we do not proactively transfer customer content to the US for processing. However, there are two caveats: (a) in rare cases we may need to route for operational reasons to alternate endpoints — we describe those exceptions in the DPA; (b) legal compulsion (e.g., valid US court order) could require disclosure.

4) Contracts & SCCs/DPA: We execute a DPA that implements EU SCCs; Marissa will share the latest DPA PDF. We can incorporate language in the DPA to clarify residency commitments for Dedicated/Private deployments and acceptable exceptions for Hosted.

5) KMS & encryption: Data at rest and in transit are encrypted. For Dedicated/Private deployments we offer an option for customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS with AWS KMS or equivalent). For Hosted accounts we offer managed keys by default and customer-managed keys on request under contractual terms.

6) Logs & retention: Application and audit logs are retained by default for 90 days. Access logs are configurable; logs do not store full customer PII as part of the standard telemetry pipeline. We can provide a log-export playbook and redaction guidance if you require longer retention or specific exclusion rules.

Next steps:
- Please confirm which deployment model WhiteCo will purchase (Hosted w/ EU residency or Dedicated/Private).
- Marissa and our legal team will prepare the DPA + bridge-letter final text for signature.
- If helpful, we can provide the list of subprocessors and an evidence package for SCC review.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Jonas and Laura — that helps. A couple quick follow-ups from our legal/security:

- We'd like the bridge letter to explicitly state there will be no transfer of customer content to locations outside the EU for processing or storage through the commitment date (2026-08-31). Can Redwood accept that exact phrase?
- If the answer is no for Hosted, please confirm you can provide Dedicated/Private as an alternative and the estimated lead time and costs for that option.
- Please share the subprocessors list and confirm whether any subprocessor has access to unredacted customer content.

I've copied procurement to start commercial discussions contingent on those answers.

Best,
Claire

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@whiteco.eu>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, procurement@whiteco.eu
Date: 2026-07-23T15:10:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence request and hosting jurisdiction

Hi Claire — Marissa from Legal & Compliance. Thanks for the clear asks. I want to be transparent: for the Hosted product we cannot unconditionally guarantee that absolutely no customer content will ever be transferred outside the EU in every theoretical scenario. The reasons are limited operational exceptions (e.g., failover, troubleshooting requiring temporary routing) and lawful requests from authorities. That said, we can offer the following contractually binding options:

1) Dedicated/Private: We can contractually guarantee EU-only hosting, EU-only control plane, and customer-managed keys. Lead time for a Dedicated deployment is typically 6-8 weeks from signed order; cost is in the Dedicated SKU and varies by committed capacity.

2) Hosted-EU residency + DPA: For Hosted customers who select EU residency we will ensure primary storage and inference processing remain in eu-central-1 and will include the EU SCCs in our DPA. We will add a contractual representation that we will not intentionally transfer customer content outside the EU for processing during the contract period except as necessary for legal compulsion or agreed failover scenarios (we can define narrow language).

3) Bridge letter: We can sign a bridge letter attesting no material changes since the SOC 2 period and extend coverage to 2026-08-31; the bridge can include the residency language above (subject to the same exceptions).

4) Subprocessors: We will provide a current list of subprocessors and a statement that subprocessors do not access unredacted customer content except under limited, audited circumstances (e.g., managed disk providers, cloud providers). We'll share that list and the subprocessors' security attestations in the evidence bundle.

Next steps: if WhiteCo needs a contract commitment that expressly prohibits any transfer under any condition, please confirm and we'll route to the executive team for discussion — that level of absolute prohibition is unusual for hosted SaaS but may be possible via Dedicated/Private procurement. Otherwise, if you're comfortable with the narrow exceptions language, we'll prepare the DPA + redlined bridge letter and a commercial proposal for Dedicated vs Hosted-EU.

Proposed timeslot for a 30-min call to finalize language: Thursday 2026-07-24 09:00-09:30 CEST or Friday 2026-07-25 14:00-14:30 CEST — please confirm.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference
